items.markingKey: D. B has 5 electrons: 1s² 2s² 2p¹.

items.stem: Which of the following contains a coordination (dative covalent) bond: C₂H₆, CH₃OH, CO and H₂O?
items.markingKey: D. In CO one atom supplies both electrons of a shared pair (e.g. N or O lone pair → H⁺, O → C in CO, N → B in H₃N–BF₃, Cl → Al in Al₂Cl₆).

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "deposition"?
options: The temperature at which the solid and liquid states of a pure substance are in equilibrium at a given pressure
The lowest possible temperature, 0 K (−273.15 °C), at which particles have minimum kinetic energy
The change from liquid to gas that occurs at the surface of a liquid at temperatures below its boiling point
The direct change of state from gas to solid
items.answer: The direct change of state from gas to solid
items.markingKey: D. "deposition" is the direct change of state from gas to solid.

items.stem: How many electrons and neutrons are present in ¹³¹I⁻? (Z = 53)
items.markingKey: D. electrons = 53 − (−1) = 54; neutrons = 131 − 53 = 78.

items.markingKey: A. Fe is [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s²; remove 4s electrons first, then 3d: [Ar] 3d⁵.

items.stem: Consider the reaction C₃H₈(g) + 5O₂(g) → 3CO₂(g) + 4H₂O(l) (burning propane in a camping stove). What mass of CO₂ produced when 36.3 g of O₂ reacts completely.
Which of the following best describes "enthalpy change (ΔH)"?
options: The energy required to break one mole of a covalent bond in gaseous molecules under standard conditions
The heat energy transferred between a system and its surroundings at constant pressure
Transfer of heat to or from the surroundings that is not measured by the calorimeter, a major systematic error
The enthalpy change when an acid and a base react to form one mole of water
items.answer: The heat energy transferred between a system and its surroundings at constant pressure
items.markingKey: B. "enthalpy change (ΔH)" is the heat energy transferred between a system and its surroundings at constant pressure.

items.stem: Which statement about sodium iodide molten is correct?
options: It conducts because its ions are free to move.
It does not conduct because it contains no charged particles.
It does not conduct because its ions are fixed in a lattice.
It conducts because it has delocalised electrons.
items.answer: It conducts because its ions are free to move.
items.markingKey: A. Conduction requires mobile charged particles; ionic compounds conduct only when molten or in solution.

items.stem: What is the main observation when a hydrocarbon burns with insufficient oxygen?
options: a colourless flame with no residue

items.stem: What is the strongest type of intermolecular force between molecules of CH₃COOH in the liquid state?
items.markingKey: D. CH₃COOH: hydrogen bonding. Covalent bonds are intramolecular, not intermolecular.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "electron affinity"?
options: The mean energy needed to break one mole of a given type of bond, averaged over many different compounds
The heat energy transferred between a system and its surroundings at constant pressure
The experimental measurement of heat transferred in a reaction from the temperature change of a known mass of a substance (usually water)
The enthalpy change when one mole of electrons is added to one mole of gaseous atoms to form one mole of gaseous 1− ions
items.answer: The enthalpy change when one mole of electrons is added to one mole of gaseous atoms to form one mole of gaseous 1− ions
items.markingKey: D. "electron affinity" is the enthalpy change when one mole of electrons is added to one mole of gaseous atoms to form one mole of gaseous 1− ions.

items.stem: The first ionisation energy of barium is 503 kJ mol⁻¹. What is the minimum energy needed to remove one electron from a single gaseous atom of barium?
items.markingKey: D. 503 × 10³ J mol⁻¹ ÷ 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹ = 8.36 × 10⁻¹⁹ J (remember kJ → J).

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "back titration"?
options: The point in a titration at which the reactants have been added in exactly the stoichiometric ratio
In a chemical reaction the total mass of the products equals the total mass of the reactants, as atoms are neither created nor destroyed
A technique in which an excess of reagent is added to the analyte and the unreacted excess is then titrated to find how much reacted
The maximum mass (or amount) of product that can be obtained from the limiting reactant, calculated from the balanced equation
items.answer: A technique in which an excess of reagent is added to the analyte and the unreacted excess is then titrated to find how much reacted
items.markingKey: C. "back titration" is a technique in which an excess of reagent is added to the analyte and the unreacted excess is then titrated to find how much reacted.

items.stem: Under which conditions does sulfur dioxide behave most like an ideal gas?
items.markingKey: B. High T: kinetic energy overcomes attractions; low p: particles far apart so their volume is negligible.

items.stem: A 25.0 g sample of stainless steel contains 8 % nickel by mass. Calculate the amount, in mol, of nickel atoms in the sample.
Which of the following best describes "gas constant (R)"?
options: A theoretical gas whose particles have negligible volume, no intermolecular forces, move randomly and undergo perfectly elastic collisions, so that it obeys pV = nRT exactly
The constant of proportionality in pV = nRT, 8.31 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹
The ratio pV/(nRT) for a gas; it equals 1 for an ideal gas
A graduated syringe used to measure volumes of gas, typically to ±0.5 cm³

items.stem: For C₂H₅OH(l) + 3O₂(g) → 2CO₂(g) + 3H₂O(l), ΔH⦵ = −1368 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔS⦵ = −138 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹. Determine the temperature below which the reaction is spontaneous.
items.markingKey: D. Set ΔG = 0: T = ΔH/ΔS (M1) = −1368/−0.138 (unit conversion) = 9910 K (A1); spontaneous below this temperature (A1).

items.stem: What is the hybridisation of the central Si atom in SiH₄?

items.stem: For the Haber process, N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g), ΔH⦵ = −92 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔS⦵ = −199 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹. What is ΔG at 1200 K?

items.stem: What is the empirical formula of glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆?

items.stem: A solid material X melts at 136 °C, dissolves in hexane and does not conduct electricity in any state. Which type of bonding and structure is X most likely to have?

m/z 10 | relative peak height 24.8
m/z 11 | relative peak height 100.0

(a) Calculate the percentage abundance of each isotope. [2]
(b) Calculate the relative atomic mass of the sample to two decimal places. [2]
(c) Identify the element from its relative atomic mass and state one reason why the value may differ slightly from the data booklet value. [2]
(d) Explain why the sample must be ionised before it can be analysed. [1]
(e) State why a small peak at half the m/z of the most abundant isotope could appear. [1]
(f) Outline one way in which the precision of the measured data could be improved. [1]
items.answer: (a) 10: 19.9 %, 11: 80.1 % (b) 10.80 (c) boron; isotopic abundances vary slightly between natural sources / peak-height measurement uncertainty. (d) Only charged particles can be accelerated and deflected (separated) by electric/magnetic fields and detected. (e) Formation of 2+ ions, which have half the m/z value. (f) Use apparatus with a smaller uncertainty (higher resolution), or increase the size of the measured quantity so the percentage uncertainty falls, and repeat trials.

(d) [1] Ions are accelerated/deflected/detected (1). (e) [1] 2+ ions (1). (f) [1] Any valid way of reducing random uncertainty: higher-resolution instrument / larger measured quantity / more repeats (1).

Electron removed | IE / kJ mol⁻¹ | log₁₀(IE)

(b) Briefly describe radiocarbon dating of the Ötzi “iceman” found in the Alps and explain what it reveals about the use of radioisotopes. [4]

items.stem:
This question is about exothermic and endothermic reactions, enthalpy profiles and standard conditions.

(a) Outline the meaning of the term "system and surroundings". [2]

(b) Distinguish between an exothermic reaction and an endothermic reaction. [4]

(c) On an energy profile, the reactants are at 300 kJ mol⁻¹, the transition state at 480 kJ mol⁻¹ and the products at 225 kJ mol⁻¹. Calculate the activation energy of the reverse reaction. [4]

(d) "Energy profiles give a complete description of a reaction." To what extent is this view justified? [5]
items.answer: (a) The system is the chemicals reacting; the surroundings are everything else, including the solvent, container and air (b) An exothermic reaction releases heat (ΔH < 0, surroundings warm up, products lower in enthalpy); an endothermic reaction absorbs heat (ΔH > 0, surroundings cool, products higher in enthalpy). (c) 255 kJ mol⁻¹ (d) They are useful summaries of energetics but not of kinetics or spontaneity in full.

(a) A student claims: "The ionisation energy of hydrogen can be found from the convergence limit of the visible (Balmer) series." Identify the error in this claim and correct it. [3]

(b) The convergence limit of the ground-state series in the spectrum of a gaseous atom occurs at a frequency of 1.21 × 10¹⁵ s⁻¹. Determine the first ionisation energy of the element in kJ mol⁻¹. [4]

(c) With the help of a specific example, explain why the convergence limit can be difficult to read directly from an emission spectrum, and how it is found in practice. [3]
items.answer: (a) The Balmer series ends at n = 2, so its convergence limit gives the energy to remove an electron from n = 2, not from the ground state; the Lyman (n = 1) series must be used. (b) 483 kJ mol⁻¹ (c) The lines become so close that they merge and cannot be resolved; the limit is found by plotting the difference in frequency between successive lines against frequency and extrapolating to zero difference. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)
items.markingKey: (a) [3 marks] The Balmer series ends at n = 2, so its convergence limit gives the energy to remove an electron from n = 2, not from the ground state; the Lyman (n = 1) series must be used. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation. (b) [4 marks] E = hf = 8.02 × 10⁻¹⁹ J (M1); IE = E × NA/1000 = 483 kJ mol⁻¹ (A1). (c) [3 marks] Award marks for: The lines become so close that they merge and cannot be resolved; the limit is found by plotting the difference in frequency between successive lines against frequency and extrapolating to zero difference. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.) (3 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

This question is about vSEPR theory: electron domain and molecular geometry.

(a) What is the bond angle in a trigonal planar molecule? [2]

(b) Felix writes: "Water is linear because it has only two bonds." Explain why this is inaccurate. [4]

(c) Explain the difference between electron domain geometry and molecular geometry. [4]
items.answer: (a) 120° (b) Water has four electron domains (two bonds, two lone pairs) in a tetrahedral arrangement; the molecule is bent (104.5°). (c) Electron domain geometry includes all domains (bonds and lone pairs); molecular geometry describes only the positions of the atoms – they differ when lone pairs are present (e.g. NH₃: tetrahedral vs trigonal pyramidal).
items.markingKey: (a) [2 marks] 120°. 360°/3. items.answer: (a) The rough titre is only a guide to the approximate end point; only concordant accurate titres are averaged. (b) 43.5 cm³ (c) 0.0691 mol dm⁻³ (d) 75.3 %

(d) [5 marks] n(HCl) total = 0.0200 mol (M1); excess n(HCl) = n(NaOH) = 0.00838 mol (M1); HCl reacted = 0.0116 mol (M1); n(CaCO₃) = ½ × = 0.00581 mol (M1); mass = 0.582 g; 75.3 % (A1).

items.stem:
This question is about entropy and predicting the sign of ΔS.

(a) Which state of matter has the highest entropy for a given substance? [2]

(b) "Entropy always decreases when a gas is cooled because ΔH is negative." Explain the flaw in this statement. [4]

(c) Using the standard entropy values (J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹) H₂O(l) 70, H₂O(g) 189, determine the standard entropy change for H₂O(l) → H₂O(g). [4]

(d) Evaluate the claim: "Counting moles of gas is a reliable way to predict the sign of ΔS for a reaction." [5]
items.answer: (a) gas (b) Entropy decreases on cooling because particles have fewer accessible energy states; the sign of ΔS is not determined by ΔH. (c) +119 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ (d) A good first approximation, but calculations with S⦵ values are needed when gas moles are equal or effects compete.
items.markingKey: (a) [2 marks] gas. Most dispersed. (b) [4 marks] Entropy decreases on cooling because particles have fewer accessible energy states; the sign of ΔS is not determined by ΔH. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation. (c) [4 marks] ΣS(products) = 189, ΣS(reactants) = 70 (M1, coefficients used); ΔS = +119 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ (A1). (d) [5 marks] Arguments for: gas entropy dominates, so the rule works for most reactions; quick qualitative prediction. Arguments against: fails when the number of gas moles is unchanged; dissolving, mixing and changes in molecular complexity also matter; quantitative ΔS requires standard entropies. Supported judgement: A good first approximation, but calculations with S⦵ values are needed when gas moles are equal or effects compete. Markbands (6 marks): IB-style extended response: 9-12 – accurate chemistry throughout, correct terminology, equations/data used to support each point, balanced evaluation and a justified conclusion; 5-8 – mostly accurate, some support, limited evaluation; 1-4 – fragmentary, largely descriptive.

(b) Distinguish between Charles's law and Boyle's law. [3]

(c) A sample of gas occupies 120 cm³ at 95.0 kPa and 20 °C. Calculate its volume at 300 kPa and 100 °C. [5]
items.answer: (a) For a fixed amount of gas at constant pressure, volume is directly proportional to absolute temperature (V/T = constant) (b) Boyle's law relates p and V at constant T (inverse proportionality); Charles's law relates V and T at constant p (direct proportionality with T in K). (c) 48.4 cm³

(a) State what is meant by the term "convergence". [2]

(b) Distinguish between a line spectrum and a continuous spectrum. [3]

(c) A student claims: "Each line in the hydrogen spectrum is produced when an electron jumps up to a higher energy level." Identify the error in this claim and correct it. [5]
items.answer: (a) The decrease in spacing between spectral lines at higher frequency, as energy levels get closer together (b) A continuous spectrum contains all wavelengths in a range; a line spectrum contains only specific wavelengths corresponding to transitions between discrete energy levels. (c) Emission lines come from electrons falling from higher to lower levels and emitting photons; promotion absorbs energy (absorption spectrum).

This question is about hess's law and enthalpy of formation and combustion cycles.

(a) "The enthalpy of formation of CO₂ is the same as the enthalpy of combustion of carbon only by coincidence." Explain the flaw in this statement. [3]

(b) Calculate the standard enthalpy of formation of C₄H₁₀(g): 4C(s) + 5H₂(g) → C₄H₁₀(g), using the enthalpies of combustion / kJ mol⁻¹: C(s) −394, H₂(g) −286, C₄H₁₀(g) −2878. [4]

(c) With the help of a specific example, explain why Hess's law follows from the law of conservation of energy. [3]
items.answer: (a) It is not coincidence: C(graphite) + O₂(g) → CO₂(g) is both the formation equation of CO₂ and the combustion equation of carbon. (b) −128 kJ mol⁻¹ (c) Enthalpy is a state function: if two routes between the same states gave different enthalpy changes, a cycle could create energy, contradicting conservation of energy. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)

This question is about theoretical, experimental and percentage yield; atom economy.

(a) A student claims: "A reaction with 100 % yield must have 100 % atom economy." Identify the error in this claim and correct it. [3]

(b) Noah carries out the thermal decomposition of limestone in a lime kiln: CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g). Starting with 47.7 g of CaCO₃ (limiting), 16.5 g of CaO is obtained. Calculate the theoretical yield and the percentage yield. [4]

(c) Calculate the atom economy for making titanium by the Kroll process: TiCl₄ + 2Mg → Ti + 2MgCl₂, where the desired product is Ti. [3]

(d) Ethanol can be manufactured by (route 1) hydration of ethene, C₂H₄ + H₂O → C₂H₅OH, with a single-pass conversion of about 5 % (unreacted ethene is recycled), or (route 2) fermentation of glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂, with a yield of about 90 %. (i) Calculate the atom economy of each route. (ii) Evaluate the two routes, considering atom economy, yield, raw materials and environmental impact. [5]
items.answer: (a) Yield and atom economy are independent: a substitution reaction can give 100 % yield but still produce by-products, so its atom economy is below 100 %. (b) 26.7 g; 61.7 % (c) 20.1 % (d) (i) route 1 100 %, route 2 51.1 %; (ii) balanced evaluation

This question is about resonance, hybridisation and sigma/pi bonds; covalent network structures.

(a) Outline the meaning of the term "delocalised electrons". [2]

(b) Explain why all the carbon–carbon bonds in benzene have the same length. [4]

(c) Draw the resonance structures of benzene, C₆H₆ and deduce the average bond order. [4]

(d) "Hybridisation is a real physical process that occurs in atoms before they bond." Discuss. [5]
items.answer: (a) Electrons shared among more than two atoms, as in benzene, carbonate or graphite (b) Six π electrons are delocalised around the ring (resonance hybrid), so each C–C bond has a bond order of 1.5 and an intermediate length between single and double bonds. (c) 2 equivalent resonance structures; bond order 1.5; electrons delocalised so all bonds identical. (d) Hybridisation is a useful model consistent with molecular shapes but not a literal physical step – an illustration of the role of models in chemistry.
